comment: Golden vectors for configuration split by signing authority. A conforming verifier must accept every case in 'cases' and refuse every case in 'reject_cases' with the declared reason at the declared stage, evaluated against the declared verifier_context. Signed with the TEST-ONLY seeds below - never use them in production. Four distinct seeds because the contract's subject is that these are different parties; a corpus sharing one could not express wrong_authority.
authority_rule: config.signing_key is matched against every configured anchor of every class, not the anchor for the document's own class. Selecting per class would report a signer writing outside its authority as a broken signature and leave wrong_authority unreachable.
envelope_note: v, class, device_id, generation, issued_at_ms and signing_key appear in every class by design. The pairwise-disjointness rule applies to payload paths, not to the envelope.
signed_over: canonical bytes of the 'config' object, not the envelope

cases.name: device_site_accepted
cases.note: The provisioning authority's document, carrying inventory and nothing that decides when a cutoff fires.

cases.name: entitlement_accepted
cases.note: The commercial policy authority's document. Its payload is the device-policy payload, verified against an anchor the provisioning authority cannot replace.

cases.name: commissioning_accepted
cases.note: The commissioning authority's document, naming the inventory generation it was commissioned against.

reject_cases.name: rated_capacity_in_a_provisioning_payload
reject_cases.note: The field this contract exists to relocate. It reads as inventory, it is in the provisioning document today, and a release-owned multiplier turns it into a trip point. Reported as foreign_field rather than malformed, so an operator is sent to the boundary rather than to a spelling mistake.

reject_cases.name: safety_multiplier_in_a_provisioning_payload
reject_cases.note: Forbidden content, which is neither a foreign field nor a typo. safety_profiles belongs to no configuration authority at all, because it is release-owned. Naming it as another authority's path would suggest moving it to a different document, and there is no document it may go in.

reject_cases.name: zones_in_a_provisioning_payload
reject_cases.note: Association, not inventory. Declaring which sensor watches which circuit is the commissioning authority's payload path.

reject_cases.name: unknown_payload_field
reject_cases.note: A field belonging to no authority is malformed rather than foreign: it is a typo or a version mismatch, and it needs a different action.

reject_cases.name: device_site_signed_by_the_commissioning_authority
reject_cases.note: The case a class-scoped selector cannot reach. Selection matches the named key across every configured anchor, so the signature verifies and the verdict is that the signer holds the wrong authority -- not that the signature is broken.

reject_cases.name: entitlement_signed_by_the_provisioning_authority
reject_cases.note: The collapse this split removes: the party that provisions a device also granting it paid capability.

reject_cases.name: signed_by_a_key_that_is_no_anchor
reject_cases.note: Self-consistent and signed by a key that is no configured anchor of any class, so no candidate can be selected and no signature is attempted.

reject_cases.name: bad_signature
reject_cases.note: Names the current provisioning key and is signed by someone who does not hold it. Selection succeeds on key material and the signature refuses.

reject_cases.name: provisioning_and_entitlement_anchors_are_identical
reject_cases.note: One party able to sign two classes is the collapse this contract prevents, and no document can reveal it. Refused at configuration load, before any document is read.

reject_cases.name: wrong_device
reject_cases.note: A document addressed to one device must never configure another.

reject_cases.name: replayed_generation
reject_cases.note: generation does not strictly exceed the accepted one for this class.

reject_cases.name: commissioning_ahead_of_inventory
reject_cases.note: A binding commissioned against an inventory generation the device has not accepted describes hardware it cannot confirm exists.

reject_cases.name: commissioning_stale_against_inventory
reject_cases.note: The seam independent application creates: a new inventory beside an old binding, every signature valid and the association silently wrong. Actuation is withdrawn until the binding is re-issued; observation and alerting continue.

reject_cases.name: legacy_document_after_the_latch
reject_cases.note: A legacy document is provisioning-signed and legitimately carries the relocated safety parameter, so replaying one after the split is an authority downgrade dressed as a valid document.
